pre_hardening.compare: the tally stage IS the pre-hardening runtime (the delivered aggregation with the committed M112 endpoint, page and analytics view), asserted identical to pre-hardening-source.json
faults: the module can aggregate the audit rows and all 26 of its own pure assertions pass, but nothing on the wire carries the count
the endpoint never calls it, so `/api/analytics` has no `rule_breaks` key at all
the page loads no card module and the analytics view mounts none, so the tally is invisible in the product

the control probe is mode-aware and measures 8/0 in every mode: on the parent it finds 0 readers and 0 mounts, on the tally-only tree 1 module that nothing calls and still 0 mounts, and on the delivered tree the three files that surface it
pre_hardening.why: On the pre-hardening runtime the unchanged probes measured pure 5/1, api 5/12, migration 2/0 and ui 4/5, and every failing line names the missing surface rather than a crash; the same assertions are `ok` on the delivered tree (79/0), and the two fault lines per probe are asserted from both texts above. The staged fault IS the parent’s own committed files.

surfaces: Views.ruleBreaks.card on the analytics view above its existing tabs
rule_breaks.scope: the resolved analysed account (the same account the payload analyses), with from/to from the payload’s own window

evidence_rules.unreadable_snapshots: a break row whose stored snapshot cannot be decoded is counted as unreadable and named, never dropped and never assumed clean
evidence_rules.unnamed_rule_events: a break row that named no rule is counted but not attributed to a rule it did not carry
evidence_rules.truncated: the bounded read is newest-first (ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT bound+1), so a bounded read is still a recent one, and truncation is flagged rather than hidden
evidence_rules.empty_but_readable: an empty readable scope answers with real zeros and by_rule:[] plus the sentence that it is a recorded tally, not a claim about unrecorded behaviour

never: a grade, cap, permission or guardrail-decision influence
a join from a break to a result

scope: M12 the rule-break tally: the aggregation of the guardrail audit the app ALREADY writes. `src/rule-breaks.js` reads `guardrail_events` back as four separate things — prevented (blocked_attempt), accepted (override), observations (breach/state_observed, a condition and NOT an attempt) and records excluded (journal_record, honest history) — and rides the review’s existing payload as `analytics.rule_breaks`, scoped to the resolved analysed account with the payload’s own window, with the UI as one read-only card. No detection was re-derived, no endpoint was added, NOTHING is written, and no grade, cap, permission or guardrail decision is influenced (the guardrail reads the live state, never this tally). Unknown stays unknown: an unreadable audit is `state:'unavailable'` with `breaks:null`, never a zero and never a clean week, and an undecodable snapshot is reported unreadable rather than assumed clean. A counted break is a RECORDED OBSERVATION and is never joined to an outcome (`outcome_joined:false`) — no 70 %/causal/predictive/broker/provider/human/mental-state/pixel/production proof, no fill padding, no sample-floor, clock, target, risk or grade retuning, and no existing guard weakened.
